w: During the darshan of Thakorji in the morning, Swamishri sprayed colored water on the murtis of Harikrishna Maharaj, Mukundanand Brahmachari, Gopinath Dev, etc. Swamishri also briefly sprayed colored water on sadhus and devotees.

This year because of the earthquake calamity, the pushpadolotsav was cancelled and only an assembly was held in the morning. In his blessings, Swamishri said, "Whatever talents we find in people have all been blessed by God... But when we acquire a talent we become arrogant. And God's talents are such that everyone experiences joy and happiness..." Then Swamishri and the assembly of sadhus and devotees offered peace prayers for the departed souls in the earthquake disaster and for the early rehabilitation of the homeless.
Swamishri then worshipped the murti of Lord Harikrishna Maharaj and sprayed a little colored water.

After Swamishri’s morning puja he gave parshad and bhagvati diksha to 42 youths. Kothari Swami placed the kanthi round each youth’s neck, Dr Swami draped a gatariyu, Mahant Swami placed a pagh and Swamishri gave the guru mantra and blessings. (For details see Swaminarayan Bliss, April 2010, inside back title.)

Today Swamishri was to give diksha to the sadhaks. On this occasion, when Swamishri came for darshan in Shastriji Maharaj's room, a sadhu sang, 'Shyam piya mori rang de chunariya...' (Dark beloved, colour my veil). This sadhu had a dark complexion. With this in mind he said, "The colour of my body is already fast, but bless me so that my heart becomes saffron."
"The colour of the body may be anything; it does not matter. What matters is devotion in the heart." Swamishri explained the greatness of inner devotion.

Doing darshan, Swamishri came into the rupchoki above the mandir. A crowd of sadhus had gathered here, some who had come from abroad and some from abroad staying here at the training centre. They all said, "To become sadhus, learn saintliness and give up our bad natures."
Swamishri said, "Grace has already been given. How much more should I give? I made you a sadhu."
Saying this, as he passed by, he said, "Everyone's natures will go."

Today thousands of devotees had gathered for the diksha ceremony. To attend, some volunteers set out from Ahmedabad early in the morning. Five volunteers of the Hirawadi area, co director Karsanbhai I. Patel, Nilkanthbhai D. Thumar, Ambarishbhai Nanjibhai Patel, Mukeshbhai Vasani and others, were coming to Sarangpur early in the morning when their car collided with a truck near Dhandhuka, and the four volunteers passed away on the spot. The fifth volunteer, Ghanshyambhai Thumar, was badly injured. Swamishri received this news while the diksha ceremony was going on, so he had the sadhus make all the arrangements.

Even at such a divine and extraordinary occasion, Swamishri did not fail to pay tribute to them in his blessings. During his blessings Swamishri said, "Today something has happened that pains us. Devotees were coming here by car, and near Dhandhuka there was an accident and four brothers left their bodies. They were coming here; they were directors. It has happened by Maharaj's wish. God is the doer; whether to keep or end a life is all God's wish. If we have that knowledge, there is no wailing. What God has done is surely good. So for this let us do a dhun today. So that their souls find peace, God keeps them happy, and there is peace in their families too, let us do a little dhun." Saying this, Swamishri himself began the dhun 'Swaminarayan... Swaminarayan...'. For about five minutes Swamishri himself led the dhun.
